recommendation.summaryForOwner: Your business shows healthy cash flow after expenses but the loans are creating pressure, especially when customers delay payments. Extending the repayment period for your existing loans can lower the monthly payment and give you more breathing room. Consider this option first, while also exploring short‑term relief if needed.

primaryRecommendation.title: Extend loan tenure by 50%
primaryRecommendation.explanation: Ask your lenders to extend the remaining loan tenure by 50% (to 50 months). This would reduce the total monthly EMI to 121855.45, giving you a larger monthly surplus of 198144.55 under normal revenue conditions.

alternativeOptions.title: 3‑month temporary payment relief
alternativeOptions.explanation: Pause EMI payments for three months; interest of 160540 will be added to the loan. After relief, the EMI becomes 174543.99, still leaving a base surplus of 145456.01.

alternativeOptions.title: Step‑down EMI plan (6 months low EMI then higher)
alternativeOptions.explanation: Pay a reduced EMI of 83100 for six months, then resume a higher EMI of 191807.27. During the low‑EMI period you would have a base surplus of 236900.

notPreferredOptions.title: Consolidate all loans into a single facility
notPreferredOptions.reasonNotPreferred: The consolidated EMI of 157127.74 only improves surplus to 162872.26, a modest benefit that does not outweigh the added complexity and higher payment.

risksAndTradeoffs: Extending tenure increases total interest paid (additional interest 1522272.5).
Longer loan duration ties up cash flow for more years.
Temporary relief may cause a larger EMI later (174543.99) and higher total interest (160540 accrued during relief).
